is_anopheles.evidence: The study tested wild Anopheles gambiae s.s. collected as larvae in Dangbo district, Benin, and the Kisumu susceptible strain (page 1, 3).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Detection of Leu–Phe kdr mutation (Vgsc L995F / L1014F) was conducted using PCR according to Martinez-Torres et al. (1998) (page 4, 5).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Page 5 reports: 'Molecular analysis of the wild Anopheles population from Dangbo showed very high frequency of kdr mutation (0.99) (49/50)'.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected as larvae from the field in Dangbo district, Benin, and reared to adults (page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical field and laboratory evaluation of insecticide formulations (page 1-4).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Ethical approval was obtained in June 2015 and the study was conducted over an 11-month period prior to submission in February 2018 (page 4, 9).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Original field trial conducted in Dangbo, Benin; no overlap with larger consortia or external surveillance datasets indicated.

supplement.evidence: The kdr frequency and sample size are reported directly in the main text on page 5.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the residual efficacy of Fludora Fusion (clothianidin + deltamethrin) against wild pyrethroid-resistant An. gambiae s.s. and susceptible Kisumu mosquitoes on cement and mud walls in Dangbo, Benin. The wild population was genotyped for the Leu-Phe kdr mutation (Vgsc L995F), showing a frequency of 0.99 (49/50).
